lines.text: Brush, brush—something old is showing through the stone.
Name the letter, name the clue, build the past bone by bone.
Start with A; arrive at Allosaurus. Allosaurus strides by | three-fingered hands and sharp teeth catch the eye
B—Brachiosaurus! Brachiosaurus was a long-necked sauropod with front legs longer than its hind legs.
inside the fossil dig, Ceratopsian catches the C beat. Ceratopsian face | beak and frill are clues to trace
What word rides with D? Deinonychus. Deinonychus was a feathered dromaeosaurid with a large sickle claw on each second toe.
Edmontosaurus, loud and clear; E brought it here. Edmontosaurus, broad bill | rows of grinding teeth worked plants still
Start with F; arrive at Footprint. A fossil footprint is a trace fossil that records where an animal stepped long ago.
G—Giganotosaurus! Giganotosaurus was a giant theropod with a huge skull and powerful hind legs.
inside the fossil dig, Hadrosaur catches the H beat. Hadrosaurs were duck-billed plant eaters with rows of closely packed grinding teeth.
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
Letter, fossil, name it—go!
What word rides with I? Irritator. Irritator in stone | fossil clues make ancient life known
Jurassic Fern, loud and clear; J brought it here. Ferns grew in many prehistoric plant communities, and fern relatives still grow today.
Start with K; arrive at Kentrosaurus. Kentrosaurus was a stegosaur with back plates toward the front and long spikes toward the rear and tail.
L—Lambeosaurus! Lambeosaurus was a duck-billed dinosaur with a tall hollow crest rising from its skull.
inside the fossil dig, Mosasaurus catches the M beat. Mosasaurus swims the sea | marine reptile—not dinosaur—our clue to see
What word rides with N? Nodosaurus. Nodosaurus was an armored plant-eating dinosaur with bony plates and no heavy tail club.
Ornithomimus, loud and clear; O brought it here. Ornithomimus runs light | long legs, small head, ostrich-like sight
Start with P; arrive at Pachycephalosaurus. Pachycephalosaurus was a two-legged dinosaur with a very thick domed skull.
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
Letter, fossil, name it—go!
Q—Qianzhousaurus! Qianzhousaurus, snout stretched long | narrow tyrannosaur profile makes the clue strong
inside the fossil dig, Rib Bone catches the R beat. Ribs form a protective cage; fossil ribs help reveal an ancient body's shape.
What word rides with S? Stegosaurus. Plates in a row | tail spikes give another clue to know
Triceratops, loud and clear; T brought it here. Triceratops was a plant-eating dinosaur with three facial horns and a large bony frill.
Start with U; arrive at Utahraptor. Utahraptor tall | giant dromaeosaur with a curved toe claw
V—Velociraptor! Velociraptor was a small feathered theropod with a curved claw on each second toe.
inside the fossil dig, Wuerhosaurus catches the W beat. Wuerhosaurus was a stegosaur with back plates and tail spikes.
What word rides with X? Xixiasaurus. Xixiasaurus was a small bird-like theropod with a slender skull and many small teeth.
Yinlong, loud and clear; Y brought it here. Yinlong on the track | fossil shapes bring the old clue back
Start with Z; arrive at Zephyrosaurus. Zephyrosaurus was a small plant-eating ornithischian with a light two-legged body.
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
Letter, fossil, name it—go!
Start with A ... land on Allosaurus! Sway one pretend tail, then freeze.
B? ... Brachiosaurus! Stretch one arm up like a long neck.
Hold the rhythm after C ... Ceratopsian! Frame a wide frill; add two horn fingers.
Last clue in the pocket: D ... Deinonychus! Curl one sickle-claw finger; take two light steps.
Start with E ... land on Edmontosaurus! Make a broad duck-bill with flat hands.
F? ... Footprint! Tap two tiny footprint beats, then show the picture.
Hold the rhythm after G ... Giganotosaurus! Show a huge head; take two heavy steps.
Last clue in the pocket: H ... Hadrosaur! Make a broad duck-bill with flat hands.
Start with I ... land on Irritator! Make a long narrow snout with two hands.
J? ... Jurassic Fern! Uncurl one hand like a fern frond, then point.
Hold the rhythm after K ... Kentrosaurus! Trace back plates; flick two tail-spike fingers.
Last clue in the pocket: L ... Lambeosaurus! Curve one hand overhead like a tall crest.
Start with M ... land on Mosasaurus! Glide one hand like a sea swimmer, then point.
N? ... Nodosaurus! Trace low armor—no tail club.
Hold the rhythm after O ... Ornithomimus! Run two long finger-legs, ostrich-style.
Last clue in the pocket: P ... Pachycephalosaurus! Make a round dome above your head.
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
Letter, fossil, name it—go!
Start with Q ... land on Qianzhousaurus! Stretch a long narrow snout forward.
R? ... Rib Bone! Brush the air gently like a fossil helper, then point.
Hold the rhythm after S ... Stegosaurus! Show a row of plates, then tail spikes.
Last clue in the pocket: T ... Triceratops! Show three horns, then frame a broad frill.
Start with U ... land on Utahraptor! Show one large toe claw; take two strong steps.
V? ... Velociraptor! Open feathered arms; curl one sickle-claw finger.
Hold the rhythm after W ... Wuerhosaurus! Trace back plates, then a tail spike.
Last clue in the pocket: X ... Xixiasaurus! Make a slender snout; take two bird-like steps.
Start with Y ... land on Yinlong! Make a small beak; take two tiny steps.
Z? ... Zephyrosaurus! Make two light running finger-steps.
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
Letter, fossil, name it—go!
Brush the stone, let the old clue show!
One last beat—our prehistoric trail comes home with me!
